cards.statement: A PodDisruptionBudget can block an administrator's direct `kubectl delete pod` request.
cards.explanation: Direct Pod deletion bypasses PodDisruptionBudget checks; use the Eviction API for budget enforcement.
cards.misconception: PodDisruptionBudgets guard direct deletion.

cards.statement: Involuntary Pod disruptions count against the available disruption budget.
cards.explanation: A failed node can consume a PodDisruptionBudget's allowance even though the budget cannot prevent the failure.

cards.statement: The Kubernetes documentation recommends `AlwaysAllow` for a PodDisruptionBudget's unhealthy Pod eviction policy.
cards.explanation: A PodDisruptionBudget using AlwaysAllow lets a drain evict unhealthy Pods instead of waiting for a misbehaving application to recover.

cards.statement: A required node affinity rule makes the kubelet evict a running Pod when node labels stop matching.
cards.explanation: A scheduled Pod continues running when node labels stop matching an `IgnoredDuringExecution` affinity rule.
cards.misconception: Node affinity ejects running Pods after label changes.

cards.statement: kube-scheduler combines separate `nodeSelectorTerms` with AND when evaluating node affinity.
cards.explanation: Matching any `nodeSelectorTerms` entry satisfies that set of node affinity terms.
cards.misconception: Separate nodeSelectorTerms are conjunctive.

cards.statement: For a Pod with `nodeSelector` and required node affinity, kube-scheduler selects a node satisfying both.
cards.explanation: A Pod with nodeSelector and required node affinity needs a node that meets both constraints.

cards.statement: NodeRestriction protects `node-restriction.kubernetes.io/` labels against changes made by the kubelet.
cards.explanation: Administrators can use these protected labels to isolate workloads on trusted nodes.

cards.statement: A Pod using `preemptionPolicy: Never` ranks below lower-priority Pods in kube-scheduler's queue.
cards.explanation: Non-preempting Pods retain their priority rank in the scheduling queue.
cards.misconception: Disabling preemption also disables priority queue ranking.

cards.statement: After kube-scheduler preempts a Pod, the kubelet honors that Pod's graceful termination period.
cards.explanation: Victim Pods get time to shut down before they disappear, creating a scheduling gap.

cards.statement: kube-scheduler moves running Pods to repair topology spread after a workload scales down.
cards.explanation: Topology spread constraints guide new placement; removing Pods can leave running Pods unevenly distributed.
cards.misconception: Topology spread constraints actively rebalance existing Pods.

cards.statement: A ClusterRoleBinding can grant a user access to a non-resource URL such as `/healthz`.
cards.explanation: The referenced ClusterRole specifies the URL and permitted request verbs.

cards.statement: An administrator can switch a RoleBinding's role by patching its `roleRef` with `kubectl patch`.
cards.explanation: `roleRef` is immutable; changing the referenced role requires deleting and recreating the binding.
cards.misconception: Existing bindings accept a different roleRef.

cards.statement: A user with Role creation and `escalate` permissions in a namespace can create Roles exceeding their own access.
cards.explanation: The escalate verb on Roles bypasses the rule-permission check at the authorized scope.

cards.statement: kube-apiserver treats permission to create RoleBindings as enough to grant access beyond the creator's permissions.
cards.explanation: Binding a Role beyond the creator's permissions needs explicit bind authorization.
cards.misconception: Creating bindings permits unrestricted role grants.

cards.statement: The control plane overwrites rules an administrator adds manually to an aggregated ClusterRole.
cards.explanation: Aggregation derives its rules from ClusterRoles matching its label selectors.

cards.statement: The default `view` ClusterRole includes read access to Secrets stored in the assigned namespace.
cards.explanation: `view` excludes Secrets because reading them can expose stronger credentials.
cards.misconception: The view role grants Secret access.

cards.statement: The default `edit` ClusterRole covers changes to Roles and RoleBindings in its target namespace.
cards.explanation: `edit` omits permissions for viewing or changing Roles and RoleBindings.
cards.misconception: The edit role includes RBAC administration.

cards.statement: By default, kube-apiserver restores missing permissions in default ClusterRoles when it starts.
cards.explanation: Startup auto-reconciliation repairs these default RBAC rules.

cards.statement: Using an RBAC `resourceNames` list grant, a client includes a matching `metadata.name` field selector.
cards.explanation: The selector confines the request to the granted resource name.

cards.statement: The client certificate in kubeadm's `admin.conf` places its user in the `system:masters` group.
cards.explanation: `admin.conf` uses `kubeadm:cluster-admins`, whose `cluster-admin` permission comes through RBAC.
cards.misconception: admin.conf uses the authorization-bypassing group.

cards.statement: A kubeadm administrator may reuse a product_uuid across nodes when their hostnames and MAC addresses differ.
cards.explanation: kubeadm's host prerequisites include unique hostname, MAC address and product_uuid values. Duplicate machine identities can cause installation failures.
cards.misconception: Distinct hostnames and MAC addresses make duplicate product_uuid values safe.

cards.statement: Before `kubeadm init`, the administrator enables host IPv4 forwarding on a Linux node used for IPv4 Pod networking.
cards.explanation: The host setup prerequisites include IPv4 packet forwarding. The administrator enables it with the net.ipv4.ip_forward sysctl during node preparation.

source.title: Container Runtimes — Enable IPv4 packet forwarding

cards.statement: `kubeadm init` asks the administrator to choose a runtime when it detects several CRI sockets on the host.
cards.explanation: Automatic runtime detection errors when kubeadm finds several runtimes. An explicit CRI socket tells kubeadm which runtime the node should use.

source.title: Installing kubeadm — Installing a container runtime

cards.statement: Docker Engine needs an administrator to install cri-dockerd before `kubeadm init` can use it as a CRI runtime.
cards.explanation: cri-dockerd supplies the CRI endpoint for Docker Engine, whose native interface does not implement Kubernetes' Container Runtime Interface.

source.title: Installing kubeadm — Installing a container runtime

cards.statement: `kubeadm init` installs the kubelet executable alongside the control plane's static Pod manifests.
cards.explanation: The administrator installs the kubelet separately. kubeadm configures an already installed kubelet while bootstrapping the cluster.
cards.misconception: Bootstrapping a control plane with kubeadm also installs the kubelet binary.

source.title: Installing kubeadm — Installing kubeadm, kubelet and kubectl

cards.statement: By default, `kubeadm init` gives the control-plane node a taint with the NoSchedule effect.
cards.explanation: The node-role.kubernetes.io/control-plane taint keeps the scheduler from placing Pods there unless they tolerate it.

source.title: Creating a cluster with kubeadm — Control plane node isolation

cards.statement: `kubeadm join` uses the discovery CA certificate hash to authenticate the joining kubelet to the control plane.
cards.explanation: The discovery hash pins the control plane's root CA public key. The TLS bootstrap token authenticates the joining node during certificate enrollment.
cards.misconception: The CA discovery hash serves as the joining kubelet's authentication credential.

source.title: kubeadm join — Token-based discovery with CA pinning

cards.statement: After `kubeadm certs renew`, the administrator restarts control plane Pods so components load renewed certificates.
cards.explanation: Manual renewal updates certificate files. Restarting the control plane Pods ensures components use the renewed credentials because certificate reload support is incomplete.

source.title: Certificate Management with kubeadm — Manual certificate renewal

cards.statement: By default, `kubeadm certs renew` rotates the cluster CA during control plane certificate renewal.
cards.explanation: kubeadm certs renew signs replacement component certificates using the existing CA. kubeadm has no built-in procedure for rotating or replacing the cluster CA.
cards.misconception: Renewing control plane certificates also replaces the certificate authority.

source.title: Certificate Management with kubeadm — Certificate authority rotation

cards.statement: `kubeadm reset` automatically clears the iptables rules that kube-proxy installs on the node for Service traffic.
cards.explanation: kubeadm reset leaves the host's kube-proxy traffic rules in place. An administrator performs any desired rule cleanup separately.
cards.misconception: Resetting a kubeadm node also removes kube-proxy's iptables rules.

source.title: kubeadm reset — Cleanup of network traffic rules

cards.statement: An administrator uses `kubeadm upgrade apply` for the first control plane node in an upgrade.
cards.explanation: The first control plane node uses kubeadm upgrade apply; later control plane nodes use kubeadm upgrade node.

cards.statement: The pkgs.k8s.io repository for the current minor release supplies packages for the next minor release.
cards.explanation: pkgs.k8s.io has a separate repository for a minor release. Switch repositories to obtain the next minor's packages.
cards.misconception: The package repository spans minor releases.

cards.statement: An administrator must drain a node before upgrading its kubelet to a new Kubernetes minor version.
cards.explanation: Draining clears evictable workloads from the node before the kubelet's minor upgrade.

cards.statement: The installed CNI plugin receives its version upgrade from `kubeadm upgrade apply`.
cards.explanation: The administrator upgrades the installed CNI plugin through its provider's procedure.
cards.misconception: kubeadm upgrades the Pod network add-on.

cards.statement: The version skew policy allows the kubelet to run up to three minor versions newer than kube-apiserver.
cards.explanation: The kubelet may be up to three minor versions older than kube-apiserver. A newer kubelet is unsupported.
cards.misconception: The kubelet's supported skew extends toward newer versions.

cards.statement: The version skew policy lets kubectl run one minor version newer or older than kube-apiserver.
cards.explanation: kubectl's supported minor-version window extends in both directions relative to kube-apiserver.

cards.statement: `etcdutl snapshot restore` sends snapshot data to a running etcd member over the network.
cards.explanation: etcdutl snapshot restore reads a local snapshot file and creates a restored data directory.
cards.misconception: etcdutl restores snapshots through a live member's API.

cards.statement: After an etcd restore to a new directory, the administrator updates the static Pod's etcd-data hostPath.
cards.explanation: Point the etcd-data hostPath in /etc/kubernetes/manifests/etcd.yaml at the restored host directory.

cards.statement: kubeadm supports HA conversion for a cluster initialized with `controlPlaneEndpoint` unset.
cards.explanation: Set the shared endpoint during kubeadm init. kubeadm does not support conversion to HA when controlPlaneEndpoint was omitted at initialization.
cards.misconception: kubeadm supports adding the shared HA endpoint after initialization.

cards.statement: In a stacked HA cluster, losing a control plane node can also take an etcd member offline.
cards.explanation: Stacked topology places an etcd member and control plane components on the same host, so host failure affects both.
